title: HeatmapR
text: addition standard distance metrics supported stats::dist(), HeatmapR also supports cosine distance hierarchical clustering. Cosine distance (1 - cosine similarity) measures angle vectors particularly useful high-dimensional data magnitude vectors less important direction. especially valuable analysing gene expression data normalised datasets.  Absolute Distance Thresholds: using cosine distance, tree_cut values 0 1 interpreted absolute cosine distance thresholds rather proportional tree heights. example, tree_cut_x = 0.5 means cluster cosine distance 0.5, 50% tree height. provides intuitive control clustering based actual distance values. Correlation distances leaf order: dist_method also accepts "pearson", "spearman" "kendall" one minus correlation, groups rows rise fall together whatever level (common gene expression), function takes matrix clustered returns dist object. dendrogram can drawn many orders, every branch can flipped; tree_order_x tree_order_y choose order. "olo" (optimal leaf ordering, Bar-Joseph, Gifford Jaakkola 2001) flips branches neighbouring rows similar possible, giving smoother gradients, "mean" orders branches mean values (stats::heatmap() uses sum leaves’ means, favours small branches).
